images.title: Too many smileys
images.purpose: Show that one smiley for every student needs far too many smileys when the numbers are large.
images.composition: One large neat grid of smileys centred, with a short label above and one line below.
images.exact_structure: Centre: a grid of exactly 35 teal #0072B2 smileys of equal size in 5 rows of 7, evenly spaced. Above it the label Class II: 35 students. Below it, in reddish purple #CC79A7, the line All 8 classes: 215 smileys. Exactly 1 grid, 35 smileys.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a grid that is not exactly 5 rows of 7
images.takeaway: One smiley for each student needs far too many smileys.
images.description: A grid of 35 smileys for one class, with a line saying all 8 classes need 215 smileys.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many smileys one class needs and why that is too many.

image_decisions.why: The problem of one symbol per student is a picture idea; one big grid shows it.
